items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication boundaries, least privilege, secrets handling, runtime isolation, release provenance and approvals, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not prove complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 35 sites pass, 14 fail, and 10 are unknown, with open consent, analytics, privacy, terms, and banner findings. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, medium for bounded growth. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; allow only reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, new data collection, cross-site exposure, monetization, or expanded claims, while continuing existing read-only evidence work. Do not claim certification or a clean bill of health.

Retain the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix. Record dated evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Use authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.
